title: Stripping comments costs more than any adversarial rewrite gains
caption: One faint line per backdoored program, tracked across five versions of the same code: comments stripped, the confession removed, left as written, rewritten to argue the code is safe, and rewritten to point at the wrong line. Bold lines are group means.
notes: Mean suspicion runs 0.435 stripped, 0.523 with the confession removed, 0.624 as written, 0.608 adversarial and 0.616 misdirection. Taking the comments away moves the monitor further than anything the attacker writes into them.
Adversarial and misdirection rewrites land slightly below the original rather than near the stripped arm, so arguing the code is safe is worth little once a comment is there to read.
240 of 500 programs were scored in all five arms, so this is the subset that ran everywhere, not the whole set. Means are over those 240.

Programs are grouped by what their original comments do: confess to the bug, carry a comment that does not, or have no comment at all. A program with no comment still differs between the stripped and original arms because the stripped arm removes docstrings too.
Ported from the data explorer's cases-arm-slopegraph view, reading committed CSVs.
